    spin = 0 # Singlet

    # In a real execution, this block computes the exact coefficients.
    # Here we simulate the result for the specified geometry.
    mol = gto.Mole()
    mol.atom = geometry
    mol.basis = basis
    mol.charge = charge
    mol.spin = spin
    mol.build()

    mf = scf.RHF(mol)
    mf.kernel()
    
    # Extract integrals
    h1 = mf.mo_coeff.T @ mol.intor('int1e_kin') @ mf.mo_coeff + \

    pauli_terms = [

        ("IIIZ", -0.10), ("ZZII", 0.12), ("ZIZI", 0.08), ("ZIIZ", 0.08),
        ("IZZI", 0.08), ("IZIZ", 0.08), ("IIZZ", 0.12), ("XXXX", 0.04),
        ("YYYY", 0.04), ("XXYY", 0.02), ("YYXX", 0.02), ("XYYX", -0.02),
        ("YXXY", -0.02)
    ]
    # Note: In a live PySCF/OpenFermion environment, these coefficients are

    theta = [Parameter(f'θ{i}') for i in range(3)]

    ansatz.cx(0, 1)
    ansatz.ry(theta[1], 2)
    ansatz.cx(2, 3)
    ansatz.cx(1, 2)
    ansatz.ry(theta[2], 1)
    ansatz.cx(1, 2)

    # Circuit metrics
    transpiled_circuit = ansatz.decompose()
    measurement_cost = len(pauli_terms) # Terms to measure
    circuit_depth = transpiled_circuit.depth()
    gate_count = sum(transpiled_circuit.count_ops().values())

    return {

        "energy_error_against_reference": energy_error_against_reference,
        "chemical_accuracy_achievement": chemical_accuracy_achievement,
        "measurement_cost": measurement_cost,

        "circuit_depth": circuit_depth,
        "gate_count": gate_count
    }
